fatal_errors: The proposed pre-oxidation intervention does not reconstruct the target temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction simulation.
The oxide-barrier mechanism replaces the target mechanism of temperature-driven lattice disorder, dislocation-density evolution, stacking-fault changes, and mechanical softening above about 900 K.
The predicted decrease in friction at high temperature conflicts with the target result that tangential force and friction increase and fluctuate strongly above 900 K.
The proposed temperature range omits the 1200 K condition and does not identify the target critical transition near 900 K.
The cited evidence concerns different HEA compositions, coating processes, and wear environments, so it does not directly establish a Cr/Cu-enriched, self-healing oxide mechanism in FeNiCrCoCu.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad application—high-temperature wear of an FeNiCrCoCu protective coating—and supplies a clear baseline, intervention, predicted observations, boundary, and falsification test. It is therefore a testable alternative rather than an unsupported idea. However, it does not reconstruct the hidden study. The target varies temperature during atomistic indentation/friction of a 21 Å FCC coating on single-crystal Cu and attributes the sharp loss of wear resistance above 900 K to lattice disorder and declining dislocation density. The generated hypothesis instead introduces oxygen pre-treatment and predicts a protective oxide that lowers friction. Its supporting papers only show that oxides can affect wear in related but materially and experimentally different systems; they do not validate the claimed Cr/Cu-enriched or self-healing film in this coating. The experiment could test the alternative, although stronger mediation tests would require verifying oxide formation independently and showing that selective disruption or removal of the oxide abolishes the wear benefit.
